REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 06/23/2024
Patient: Fatou Bryant, 30F

CC: weak, tired, dark urine.

HPI: 30-year-old woman with SLE, lupus nephritis and a prior episode of autoimmune pericarditis. For about a week she has felt progressively more tired and weak, with headaches that come and go. Urine has been dark for two days. No recent infections. No medication changes.

Home meds: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, vitamin D3, calcium carbonate. NKDA.

Vitals on arrival: afebrile, BP 150/90, HR 110.
Exam: jaundiced, scleral icterus. Mildly confused, slow to answer and has trouble concentrating. No focal weakness. Heart tachycardic, regular. Lungs clear.

Labs: Hgb 7.0, platelets 20,000, LDH 600, haptoglobin <10, creatinine 2.5. Smear: numerous schistocytes. INR normal. Urine hCG negative.

MDM: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with severe thrombocytopenia, renal involvement and neurologic symptoms in a patient with SLE. TTP must be excluded; ADAMTS13 sent. Hematology consulted from the ED; plasma exchange to start tonight. Admitted to medicine.

ED diagnoses (coded): Thrombocytopenia. Anemia. Senile purpura. Systemic lupus erythematosus.

Disposition: admitted, stepdown.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 06/23/2024  Discharged 06/28/2024
Patient: Fatou Bryant, 30F
Attending service: hospital medicine; consultants hematology, rheumatology, nephrology.

Reason for admission: microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with platelets 20,000, creatinine 2.5 and confusion in a patient with SLE and lupus nephritis.

Hospital course:
TTP was the immediate concern. Daily therapeutic plasma exchange began the night of admission, along with IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for three doses. ADAMTS13 activity returned on 06/25 at 52%, which argues against TTP, and plasma exchange was stopped after the third session. Hemolysis and thrombocytopenia were attributed to active lupus. Antiphospholipid testing was repeated: lupus anticoagulant not detected, anticardiolipin and anti-beta-2 glycoprotein I antibodies negative. Headache and confusion cleared by hospital day 2 and the remaining neurologic exam was normal. Jaundice faded. Platelets and hemoglobin rose steadily after steroids; no transfusion needed. Creatinine improved with treatment of the flare. Blood pressure normalized as she improved.

Discharge data: platelets 138,000, hemoglobin 8.4, creatinine 1.4.

Discharge diagnoses: SLE flare with microangiopathic hemolysis and thrombocytopenia; lupus nephritis.

Discharge medications:
- Prednisone 60 mg daily; rheumatology to direct the taper.
- Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID (continue).
- Vitamin D3 2000 units daily, calcium carbonate 600 mg BID (continue).
Stopped: prednisone 5 mg (replaced by above).

Follow-up: PCP within one week (CBC, BMP, hepatic panel). Hematology in 6 weeks. Rheumatology in 2 weeks.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pt texted Monday that she was admitted. Spoke with the hospitalist today. ADAMTS13 back at 52%, so not TTP; plasma exchange stopping. On pulse steroids, counts climbing. Mental status back to normal. Expect discharge late this week. Asked for summary to be faxed and arranged TCM visit for 7/2. Cancelled her 6/25 follow-up here.

Plasma exchange x3 and pulse methylpred; ADAMTS13 52%, not TTP. aPL panel again negative. Discharge plt 138k, Hgb 8.4, Cr 1.4. Discharge summary and ED record reviewed and reconciled.

Today: tired but much better than last week. No headache, thinking clear. Urine normal color. No bruising or bleeding. Eating a lot on prednisone 60, sleeping poorly. Out of work this week and next.

Meds reconciled: prednisone 60 mg daily (taper per rheum, appointment 7/8), HCQ 200 BID, D3 2000 units, calcium carbonate 600 BID.

Exam: vitals as charted, BP normal. No icterus. No petechiae. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Neuro: alert, oriented, fluent, no focal deficit. No edema.

A/P
1. SLE flare with hemolysis and thrombocytopenia, recovering. CBC, BMP, hepatic panel today; results to hematology and rheum.
2. Lupus nephritis - creatinine improving.
3. High-dose steroids: glucose on BMP. Discussed sleep, appetite, mood.
4. Work note through 7/15.
RTC after taper or sooner.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL — NEPHROLOGY SERVICE DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 04/27/2025 via the emergency department. Discharged 04/30/2025.
Patient: Fatou Bryant, 31F. NKDA.

Presentation: Three days of severe vomiting and diarrhea, unable to keep fluids down, much like the illness that brought her to the ED last October. For abdominal cramping she had been taking ibuprofen every 4 hours.
On arrival BP 90/60, HR 110. Lethargic, mucous membranes dry, poor skin turgor.

Data: creatinine 2.1 (baseline 0.9), BUN 40, potassium 3.5, bicarbonate 24. Urine sodium 10, urine osmolality 500.

Assessment: acute kidney injury, prerenal from volume depletion, with NSAID use contributing; dehydration from gastrointestinal losses.

Course: IV isotonic fluids, antiemetics, ibuprofen stopped. Hydroxychloroquine and prednisone continued. Diarrhea settled by day 2, tolerating diet day 3. Creatinine 1.1 on the morning of discharge.

Discharge medications: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, vitamin D3, calcium carbonate. STOP ibuprofen and all NSAIDs; acetaminophen for pain.
Follow-up: PCP within one week with BMP. Nephrology clinic as scheduled.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after nephrology admission 4/27-4/30 for prerenal AKI (Cr 2.1, BUN 40, UNa 10, Uosm 500) from vomiting/diarrhea plus ibuprofen every 4 hours. Discharge Cr 1.1. Summary reviewed.

Feels back to normal. Eating and drinking fine, no GI symptoms since day 2. No ibuprofen since. She didn't realize ibuprofen mattered for her kidneys when she was sick; she had been told to avoid it but took it because the cramping was bad. Talked it through again without blame: acetaminophen only; call us early when she can't keep fluids down so we can see her same day or arrange fluids before it gets to this.

Exam: vitals as charted, BP normal. Mucous membranes moist. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema.

A/P
1. AKI - resolved clinically; BMP today to confirm.
2. Dehydration - resolved.
3. NSAID avoidance added to the chart alert and med list; ibuprofen removed.
4. SLE, lupus nephritis - stable.
RTC for physical in August.

documents.title: Kidney test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your creatinine is back to your normal. Kidneys have fully recovered. Remember: acetaminophen (Tylenol) only for pain, and message me early if you get another stomach bug.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 10/23/2025  Discharged 10/29/2025
Patient: Fatou Bryant, 32F. NKDA.
Consultants: hematology, rheumatology.

Reason for admission: second episode of microangiopathic hemolysis with platelets 20,000 and hemoglobin 7.8 in SLE; epistaxis.

Course: Plasma exchange was started on arrival while ADAMTS13 was pending, with IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily x 3. ADAMTS13 activity resulted 58% on 10/25; TTP excluded and plasma exchange stopped after two sessions. Antiphospholipid antibodies again negative. Hematology and rheumatology agree this is recurrent lupus-related hemolysis with thrombocytopenia, same as June 2024. No further nosebleeds after day 1. No transfusion. Hemolysis markers improved through the stay. Creatinine stayed near baseline.

Discharge data: platelets 146,000, hemoglobin 8.9.

Discharge medications: prednisone 60 mg daily with rheumatology-directed taper; hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID; vitamin D3 2000 units; calcium carbonate 600 mg BID. Prednisone 5 mg stopped (replaced). Continue to avoid NSAIDs.
